title: B-17 Flying Fortress – Regensburg Raid
subtitle: WWII Era, August 17, 1943
summary: The Boeing B-17F Flying Fortress was a critical asset in the U.S. Army Air Forces’ strategic bombing campaign during World War II. This digital painting depicts the 91st Bomb Group on August 17, 1943, flying into Regensburg as part of Operation Double Strike, facing intense Luftwaffe resistance.
notableFact: First unescorted shuttle raid to North Africa

title: P-38 Lightning – Bismarck Sea Patrol
subtitle: WWII Era, March 2-4, 1943
summary: The Lockheed P-38 Lightning was a versatile twin-engine fighter that excelled in reconnaissance and long-range escort missions. This digital painting depicts the 39th Fighter Squadron patrolling the Bismarck Sea during the Battle of the Bismarck Sea, crippling an enemy convoy.
notableFact: First fighter to shoot down an enemy aircraft on December 7, 1941

title: Spitfire Mk IX – Overlord Escort (JE-J)
subtitle: WWII Era, June 1, 1944
summary: The Supermarine Spitfire Mk IX was deployed during the critical months leading up to the D-Day invasion. This artwork captures Spitfire Mk IX 'JE-J' in flight above the Normandy coast on June 1, 1944, part of a defensive sweep to ensure Allied operational security.
armament: Two 20mm Hispano cannons, four .303 machine guns
notableFact: Key defender in D-Day preparations

title: P-51 Mustang – D-Day Escort
subtitle: WWII Era, June 6, 1944
summary: The North American P-51D Mustang was a game-changer in World War II, renowned for its long-range capabilities and agility. This digital painting captures the 352nd Fighter Group on June 6, 1944, escorting bombers over Normandy during the D-Day invasion.
notableFact: Longest-range fighter escort of WWII

title: Republic P-47 Thunderbolt
subtitle: WWII Era, April 8, 1944
summary: The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt was a rugged, heavily armed fighter used by the U.S. Army Air Forces during World War II. This digital painting depicts a P-47 Thunderbolt from the 56th Fighter Group on April 8, 1944, strafing German positions during the Battle of the Bulge.
notableFact: One of the heaviest single-engine fighters of WWII

title: Messerschmitt Bf 109
subtitle: WWII Era, 1940
summary: The Messerschmitt Bf 109 was a German World War II fighter aircraft, renowned as the backbone of the Luftwaffe. This digital painting depicts a Bf 109E from Jagdgeschwader 26 in 1940, engaged in combat during the Battle of Britain.
notableFact: Most produced German fighter of WWII

title: Focke-Wulf FW 190
subtitle: WWII Era, 1943
summary: The Focke-Wulf FW 190 was a German WWII fighter, renowned for its speed, firepower, and versatility. This digital painting depicts an FW 190 from Jagdgeschwader 2 in 1943, engaging in combat over the Western Front.
notableFact: Known as the 'Butcher Bird' for its lethality

title: Grumman F6F Hellcat
subtitle: WWII Era, 1943
summary: The Grumman F6F Hellcat was a U.S. Navy carrier-based fighter that dominated the Pacific Theater during World War II. This digital painting depicts an F6F-3 Hellcat from VF-9 aboard USS Essex in 1943, engaging enemy aircraft during the Battle of the Philippine Sea.
notableFact: Achieved a 19:1 kill ratio against Japanese aircraft

title: Hawker Hurricane
subtitle: WWII Era, September 1940
summary: The Hawker Hurricane was a British fighter aircraft that played a pivotal role in the Battle of Britain during World War II. This digital painting depicts a Hurricane Mk I from No. 303 Squadron (Polish) in September 1940, engaging Luftwaffe fighters over London.
notableFact: Shot down more enemy aircraft than the Spitfire during the Battle of Britain

title: Hawker Typhoon
subtitle: WWII Era, 1944
summary: The Hawker Typhoon was a British fighter-bomber used during World War II, renowned for its powerful engine and effectiveness in ground-attack roles. This digital painting depicts a Typhoon Mk IB from No. 56 Squadron in 1944, attacking German armor in Normandy.
armament: Four 20mm cannons, eight 60 lb rockets or 2,000 lb bombs
notableFact: Nicknamed ‘Tiffy’ by pilots

title: Consolidated B-24 Liberator
subtitle: WWII Era, 1943
summary: The Consolidated B-24 Liberator was a heavy bomber used by the U.S. Army Air Forces in World War II, known for its long range and heavy payload. This digital painting depicts a B-24D from the 93rd Bomb Group in 1943, bombing Ploesti oil fields in Romania.
engine: Four Pratt & Whitney R-1830 Twin Wasp
notableFact: More B-24s were built than any other American bomber

title: Avro Lancaster
subtitle: WWII Era, 1943
summary: The Avro Lancaster was a British heavy bomber that became the backbone of the RAF’s night bombing campaign during World War II. This digital painting depicts a Lancaster B I from No. 617 Squadron in 1943, during the Dambusters raid on German dams.
armament: Eight .303 machine guns, up to 14,000 lb bombs
notableFact: Famous for the Dambusters raid using bouncing bombs

title: Boeing B-29 Superfortress
subtitle: WWII Era, August 1945
summary: The Boeing B-29 Superfortress was a four-engine heavy bomber developed by the United States during World War II, renowned for its advanced technology. This digital painting depicts a B-29 from the 509th Composite Group in August 1945, dropping the atomic bomb on Hiroshima.
armament: Ten .50-caliber machine guns, 20,000 lb bomb load
notableFact: Delivered the first atomic bombs

title: Junkers Ju 88
subtitle: WWII Era, 1941
summary: The Junkers Ju 88 was a versatile German aircraft used as a bomber, dive bomber, and reconnaissance plane during World War II. This digital painting depicts a Ju 88 A-4 from Kampfgeschwader 30 in 1941, attacking Allied shipping in the Arctic convoys.
notableFact: One of the most versatile aircraft of WWII

title: Mitsubishi G4M 'Betty'
subtitle: WWII Era, 1942
summary: The Mitsubishi G4M, nicknamed 'Betty,' was a Japanese twin-engine bomber used by the Imperial Japanese Navy during World War II. This digital painting depicts a G4M1 from the Kanoya Air Group in 1942, attacking Allied ships during the Battle of the Coral Sea.
armament: Four 7.7mm machine guns, one 20mm cannon, 2,200 lb bombs or torpedo
notableFact: Nicknamed ‘Betty’ by Allied forces

title: Douglas C-47 Skytrain
subtitle: WWII Era, June 1944
summary: The Douglas C-47 Skytrain, a military variant of the DC-3, was a vital transport aircraft for the Allies in World War II. This digital painting depicts a C-47 from the 101st Airborne Division in June 1944, dropping paratroopers over Normandy on D-Day.
engine: Two Pratt & Whitney R-1830 Twin Wasp
notableFact: Carried paratroopers on D-Day

title: De Havilland Mosquito
subtitle: WWII Era, 1944
summary: The De Havilland Mosquito was a British multi-role aircraft of World War II, known for its wooden construction, speed, and versatility. This digital painting depicts a Mosquito B Mk IV from No. 627 Squadron in 1944, conducting a low-level precision bombing raid over Germany.
notableFact: Fastest Allied bomber of its time

title: Martin B-26 Marauder
subtitle: WWII Era, 1943
summary: The Martin B-26 Marauder was a U.S. medium bomber used during World War II, known for its speed and low loss rate despite early handling challenges. This digital painting depicts a B-26B from the 323rd Bomb Group in 1943, bombing German supply lines in France.
engine: Two Pratt & Whitney R-2800 Double Wasp
notableFact: Had the lowest loss rate of any Allied bomber

title: F-86 Sabre – MiG Alley Dogfight
subtitle: Korean War, September 15, 1952
summary: The North American F-86F Sabre was a cornerstone of U.S. air power during the Korean War, renowned for its agility and effectiveness against Soviet MiG-15s. This digital painting captures the 335th Fighter-Interceptor Squadron on September 15, 1952, engaging MiG-15s over MiG Alley.
notableFact: First swept-wing fighter in USAF service

title: English Electric Canberra
subtitle: Cold War, 1956
summary: The English Electric Canberra was a British first-generation jet bomber, known for its high-altitude performance and versatility during the early Cold War era. This digital painting depicts a Canberra B.2 from No. 101 Squadron in 1956, during the Suez Crisis.
notableFact: First British jet bomber in service

title: Dassault Mirage III
subtitle: Cold War, 1978
summary: The Dassault Mirage III was a French supersonic fighter and interceptor, widely used during the Cold War for its agility and advanced avionics. This digital painting depicts a Mirage IIIE from the Royal Australian Air Force’s No. 75 Squadron in 1978.
notableFact: First Western European jet to exceed Mach 2

title: North American F-100 Super Sabre
subtitle: Vietnam War, 1965
summary: The North American F-100 Super Sabre was a U.S. Air Force jet fighter, notable as the first USAF aircraft capable of supersonic speed in level flight. This digital painting depicts an F-100D from the 20th Fighter Wing in 1965, conducting a close air support mission during the Vietnam War.
notableFact: First USAF fighter to exceed Mach 1 in level flight

title: Tupolev Tu-95 'Bear'
subtitle: Cold War, 1965
summary: The Tupolev Tu-95 'Bear' is a Soviet strategic bomber and reconnaissance aircraft, known for its distinctive turboprop engines and long-range capabilities during the Cold War. This digital painting depicts a Tu-95 from the Soviet Long-Range Aviation in 1965, conducting a maritime patrol over the Atlantic.
armament: Two 23mm cannons, up to 33,000 lb bombs or missiles
notableFact: Longest-serving strategic bomber still in use

title: Lockheed U-2
subtitle: Cold War, 1960
summary: The Lockheed U-2, nicknamed 'Dragon Lady,' is a U.S. high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft, pivotal during the Cold War for its ability to gather intelligence over hostile territory. This digital painting depicts a U-2 from the 9th Reconnaissance Wing in 1960, flying over Cuba during the Cuban Missile Crisis.
notableFact: Flew at altitudes above 70,000 ft

title: Gloster Meteor
subtitle: WWII Era, 1945
summary: The Gloster Meteor was the first British jet fighter and the Allies’ only operational jet aircraft during World War II, marking the dawn of the jet age. This digital painting depicts a Meteor F.3 from No. 616 Squadron in 1945, intercepting V-1 flying bombs over England.
notableFact: First Allied jet fighter in combat

title: F4U Corsair – Rabaul Strike Run
subtitle: WWII Era, February 19, 1944

notableFact: First carrier-based fighter to exceed 400 mph

title: Mitsubishi A6M Zero
subtitle: WWII Era, December 1941

notableFact: Symbol of Japanese air power in early WWII

title: Douglas SBD Dauntless
subtitle: WWII Era, June 1942
summary: The Douglas SBD Dauntless was a U.S. Navy dive bomber that played a critical role in the Pacific Theater of World War II, particularly at the Battle of Midway. This digital painting depicts an SBD-5 from VB-16 aboard USS Lexington in June 1942, diving on Japanese carriers at Midway.
armament: Two .50-caliber machine guns, two .30-caliber machine guns, 2,250 lb bombs
notableFact: Sank four Japanese carriers at Midway

title: Fairey Swordfish
subtitle: WWII Era, 1941
summary: The Fairey Swordfish was a British biplane torpedo bomber used by the Royal Navy during World War II. This digital painting depicts a Swordfish from 820 Naval Air Squadron in 1941, attacking the German battleship Bismarck.
armament: One 18-inch torpedo or 1,500 lb bombs, two .303 machine guns
notableFact: Crippled the Bismarck with a torpedo hit

title: Douglas A-1 Skyraider
subtitle: Korean War, 1953
summary: The Douglas A-1 Skyraider was a U.S. Navy and Marine Corps attack aircraft, known for its versatility and heavy payload. This digital painting depicts an AD-4 Skyraider from VA-115 in 1953, conducting close air support during the Korean War.
armament: Four 20mm cannons, up to 8,000 lb bombs/rockets
notableFact: Nicknamed ‘Spad’ for its ruggedness

title: Goodyear F2G Corsair
subtitle: WWII Era, 1945
summary: The Goodyear F2G Corsair was a supercharged variant of the F4U Corsair, designed for enhanced performance. Developed late in World War II, it saw limited use but showcased advanced engineering.
notableFact: Supercharged variant with limited production

title: Fieseler Fi 156 Storch
subtitle: WWII Era, 1940
